newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan bourse to sign automation deal in two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Jordan bourse to sign automation deal in two weeks.

text.p: Jordan expects to sign a contract within two weeks with the French government to fully automate trading on the Amman stock exchange, bourse director general Umayya Toukan said on Thursday.
He said the new system, expected to be financed by French government grants, could be up and running withing 14 months of the deal being signed.
It would settle deals instantly, replacing a laborious trading and clearing system which currently takes three days to settle transactions.
"We hope to get into the 21st century with a highly competitive stock exchange in Jordan," said Toukan, who leaves his post as head of the Amman Financial Market in mid-October."
"The new system will transfer title of ownership and settle payments instantly," he told Reuters. "It should be a very positive factor in attracting international interest."

Toukan said the new settlement system was part of a wider package of reforms aimed at making the market, on a downward trend for two years after a 1992-93 bull run, more transparent, efficient, and investor-friendly.

A draft law is due to be put before Jordan's parliament soon which would tighten up regulations on accountability and transparency both for brokers and listed companies on the Amman Financial Market (AFM).
It will also toughen up rules against insider dealing, and separate the regulatory role of the AFM from its day-to-day trading supervision.
"It's a highly sophisticated piece of legislation which will upgrade the Jordanian market and make it competitive with developed markets," Toukan said.

The Amman exchange, one of the most politically sensitive bourses in the region, was hit this year by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq.
Already suffering from high domestic interest rates, market capitalisation fell nine percent to 2.9 billion dinars ($4.1 billion) at the end of July from 3.2 billion at the start of the year.
Toukan, who has run the exchange since 1991, will hand over on October 15 to Wahib Shair, senior national partner at Allied Accountants, a member firm of Arthur Andersen and Co.
